topic: TrueForge: The Open-Source Agent Harness for Reproducible Agent Runs

key_points: Primary source: TrueForge is the open-source agent harness from TrueFoundry — the runtime layer that turns an LLM into a working agent
Runs the full agent execution loop: model calls, MCP tools, skills, sandboxing, approvals, context management, and session state
Exposed three ways: bundled chat UI, HTTP API with TypeScript SDK, and embeddable React UI SDK
MIT license, TypeScript, ~5,038 stars / 348 forks, created 2026-07-23, homepage trueforge.dev
Two run modes: local (single process, SQLite) and hosted (Postgres + Redis, Docker Compose, Helm, or Railway)
Benchmarked against Claude Managed Agents (closed) and deepagents (open-source, LangGraph) on the same 14 enterprise tasks, same tools, same model
~30% cheaper than Claude Managed Agents on the same model (Opus 4.8); ~2.5x cheaper than deepagents; ~75% cheaper running GLM-5.2 at same quality
Uses L1-L2 tasks from DevRev's Enterprise-Bench — 14 cross-system tasks joining data across three MCP servers (CRM, project tracker, document store)
n=3 trials per config, graded by independent LLM judge blind to which harness produced the answer
Results: CMA·Opus 10.7/14 $11.8 10.0M tokens; TrueForge·Opus 10.7/14 $8.6 3.7M; TrueForge·GLM-5.2 11.7/14 $3.0 3.8M; deepagents·Opus 10.0/14 $21.2 16.5M; deepagents·GLM-5.2 12.0/14 $9.1 11.9M
Defines an agent harness as the runtime layer around an LLM that turns it into a reliable, long-running agent

Harness runs the full execution loop: planning, tool routing and execution, context management for long tasks, security boundaries (sandboxing, human-in-the-loop approvals), and session state that survives reconnects/restarts
TrueForge has three parts: core server running the agent loop, HTTP API (TypeScript SDK) to drive from code, and chat UI (React UI SDK) to drive from browser
Key components: TrueForge server, HTTP API + TypeScript SDK, Chat UI + UI SDK, SQLite or Postgres storage, bring-your-own models/MCP servers/sandbox
HN Show/launch thread: 'TrueForge – The open-source agent harness', 23 points, ~6 comments, posted 2026-08-20
Community questions: why use this instead of more well-established open-source agent harnesses; can I bring models from OpenRouter to experiment
Signals the competitive positioning question against established harnesses (deepagents, LangGraph, Claude Managed Agents)

Planned directions: gateway integration (pull model providers and MCP servers from a gateway like TrueFoundry), local mode improvements, smarter harness, agent authoring and management, approvals and governance, evaluation
Roadmap is directional, not a committed schedule — priorities may change
Signals active investment in governance/approvals and evaluation, relevant for enterprise adoption

stats.fact: TrueForge is ~30% cheaper than Claude Managed Agents on the same model (Opus 4.8) at the same accuracy (10.7/14 tasks solved)
TrueForge is ~2.5x cheaper than deepagents (LangGraph) on the same model — $8.6/run vs $21.2/run on Opus 4.8
Running the efficient open model GLM-5.2, TrueForge is ~75% cheaper at the same quality (11.7/14 solved, $3.0/run)
TrueForge used the fewest tool calls of the three harnesses to reach the same result — 19 per task, versus 32 and 40
TrueForge repo has ~5,038 GitHub stars and 348 forks as of 2026-09-01, MIT-licensed, written in TypeScript
TrueForge was created 2026-07-23 and is actively developed (latest releases 0.2.0-rc.0 / 0.3.0-rc.0 on 2026-08-27)
@truefoundry/trueforge npm package had 3,470 downloads and @truefoundry/trueforge-sdk had 4,249 downloads in the last month (2026-07-31 to 2026-08-29)
TrueForge supports any model provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and other catalog providers, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint

angles: The 'harness' concept: building an agent is easy, running one well is not — TrueForge packages the hard runtime layer (streaming, session persistence, tool servers, sandboxing, approvals, UI) out of the box

Cost efficiency is the headline differentiator: same accuracy at ~30% cheaper than Claude Managed Agents and ~2.5x cheaper than deepagents, driven by leaner context, fewer tool calls, and compaction instead of replay
Open-source vs closed: TrueForge is MIT-licensed and self-hostable (local SQLite or hosted Postgres/Redis), contrasting with closed Claude Managed Agents
Bring-your-own-everything: any model provider, MCP servers, skills (git-backed SKILL.md), and sandbox (Daytona today, more planned) — a modular, vendor-neutral harness
Enterprise governance angle: human checkpoints (tool approval, ask-user-questions, Generative UI), OIDC login for shared deployments, and a roadmap focused on approvals/governance and evaluation
Reproducibility: benchmark kit on GitHub lets you reproduce the cost/accuracy results yourself — a strong trust signal for a review piece
Rapid momentum: launched 2026-07-23, ~5k stars in ~6 weeks, active rc releases — a fast-moving young project worth evaluating
